summary.intent: Finish trail #176 (release-command precondition fixes) by committing, pushing and linking it to a PR, then start trail #177 so that CLI error envelopes carry the subcommand path and `dryRun`, as the success reports do.
summary.outcome: Trail #176 was committed, pushed, linked, and PR #428 was updated. For trail #177, the error envelope now includes the command path and `dryRun`, with new unit and e2e tests and extended REL-CMD-12 and REL-PR-07 spec criteria. A changeset was added and clippy passes. `cargo fmt` was run, but its final check result is not shown, and the work is not yet committed or pushed.

repo: Commits and PRs follow conventional-commit style (`fix(release): ...`). Each change gets a `.changeset` entry, and behavior changes are tied to spec IDs in `docs/specs/release.json` (e.g. REL-CMD-04, REL-AUTH-05).
Pre-push checks are `cargo clippy --offline -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`, plus per-crate tests run with `--offline`.
Trails are linked with `entire trail link <n> --repo --project --branch --base`, and the PR body references the trail URL.
Git operations use `/usr/bin/git` explicitly. Work happens in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners`.
Integration tests build the CLI via `tests/common/release_harness.rs` (`callisto` helper).
The origin tag probe must use the quiet runner and not the live-echoing one, and a unit test enforces this.

code.finding: `format_error_json` builds the JSON error envelope. It now takes the command path and `dryRun`, and its doc comment and shape test were updated to match.

Report names are derived from the parsed CLI. A new unit test checks the command-path naming across release subcommands, using `try_parse_from` so a clap usage error is reported instead of exiting the process.
REL-CMD-12 and REL-PR-07 were extended so the spec covers error envelopes as well as success reports.

workflow: Use `try_parse_from` rather than `parse_from` in clap tests, because `parse_from` exits the process on a usage error and hides which invocation was wrong.
Dry-run tests probe registries and fail inside the sandbox, which blocks the network. Re-run those tests outside the sandbox before treating a failure as a regression.
After a change to a shared output shape such as the error envelope, run the full integration suite to catch exact-match assertions elsewhere.
Filtering test output too aggressively can hide the panic message. Fall back to `tail` when the grep shows nothing useful.

friction: Several test runs needed repeated grep and tail variations to surface failure details, because the filters dropped the panic message.
`test_full_polyglot` failed in the sandbox because of blocked network access, which looked like a regression until it was re-run outside the sandbox.
A clap usage error in the new unit test exited the test binary and took several iterations to locate.
The e2e test file `error_envelope_tests.rs` needed multiple edit and re-run cycles before it passed.
